newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: GOLF-HAMANO TAKES OVER LEAD AT MALAYSIAN OPEN.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-HAMANO TAKES OVER LEAD AT MALAYSIAN OPEN.

text.p: Japan's Harumitsu Hamano took over the lead in the third round of the Malaysian Open on Saturday.
His 66 added to his earlier rounds of 71 and 67, for a total of 12-under 204.

Hamano, together with tied second round leaders American Larry Barber and Lee Westwood of Britain, shot eagles on the daunting par-five 14th hole, the first time this has happened at the Malaysian Open.
Hamano bagged his eagle by hitting an 80-yard wedge over the trees to the unsighted cup.
Westwood, who was joint leader after 36 holes, scored his eagle with a 35-foot putt.
Barber, a son of Miller Barber, a former leading pro now in the senior ranks, holed out from a bunker.
Hamano snatched the lead on the strength of a birdie on the 16th. He last played in the Open nine years ago where he finished runner-up to American Tray Tyner.
